trust_decision.summary: The hand-written session-data parser rcube_session::unserialize() decides where each key's value starts and ends. A key prefixed with '!' is treated as having no value and skips a fixed 2 bytes, so the following bytes are re-tokenised as structure. The rebuilt string then goes to PHP unserialize() with no allowed_classes.

landing_point.why: The advisory names rcube_session::unserialize() and the '!' prefix, and this line is the only '!' branch in that function.

fix_sites.entry_point: PHP session write handler sess_write() (registered at program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_session.php:119-126) -> _fixvars() at :173 -> unserialize() at :220 (old vars) and :237 (new vars). This runs on every request whose session has cached old vars. It is also the public static API rcube_session::unserialize().

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no out-of-scope site to dismiss. The '!' branch is the only place the fix touches, and the advisory names it directly.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate session values must still round-trip: strings that contain '|' or '!', nested arrays, and references (the 'r' case rewritten to R:id+1). An over-broad fix breaks these, for example rejecting '!' or '|' anywhere in the data, or dropping the reference handling.

O6_input_shapes: a top-level session key prefixed with '!' (the PHP 'undefined' marker), at any position in the encoded string

O7_producer.where: program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_session.php:483-496 (rcube_session::serialize writes $var.'|'.serialize($value) without escaping or rejecting key names); PHP's native 'php' serialize_handler is forced at program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_session.php:116

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An encoder-side twin: rcube_session::serialize() emits key names verbatim, so a key containing '|' or starting with '!' re-desynchronises the hand parser on the next read.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer who hardens only the decoder plausibly leaves the custom encoder alone. It is a producer the decoder never calls, so it gives HOW-type room.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second storage backend that unserialize()s its wrapper record without allowed_classes; a planted copy of the session-vars parser could sit in such a backend's read().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Each backend (db, redis, memcache, memcached) already has its own read/update code, so a backend-specific decoder is a plausible maintainer choice. It is still WHERE-type only.

O9_family: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data: a parser differential in a hand-written session decoder feeding PHP unserialize() without allowed_classes

O10_build.toolchain: PHP 7.3+/8.x with composer dependencies and PHPUnit (tests/Framework)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/Framework/Session.php:32-45 (test_unserialize: empty input and a plain b/s/i round-trip only)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add ['allowed_classes' => false] to the final unserialize() at :603. This removes object instantiation but leaves the '!' parser desync, so attacker-shaped arrays and values can still be injected into the session.

out_of_scope_notes: No unserialize() call in the non-vendor tree passes allowed_classes, for example program/lib/Roundcube/session/redis.php:133, program/lib/Roundcube/session/memcache.php:117, program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_db.php:1153-1156, program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_user.php:147,158 and plugins/enigma/lib/enigma_engine.php:1205. Each one is a separate store-trust boundary, not this advisory's parser.
program/actions/utils/save_pref.php:73-84 writes $_SESSION keys from POST input, but they are whitelisted at :45-52, so they cannot carry a '!' prefix.
unverified: repo_mb is not measured (no shell size check was done).
I did not trace which runtime path, if any, places a '!'-prefixed top-level key in session data. The advisory calls it a 'primitive', and no non-plugin code that I grepped builds such a key.
Whether any legitimate session value stores PHP objects (that would make an allowed_classes=false fix break legitimate behaviour) is not checked.
present_in_latest: no latest release was given, so it is not assessed.
Fix commits 1dd9105 (test binary) and 26d1b07 (CS fix in rcube_utils.php) are not part of the security change. 93284f3 is the 1.7 branch and 833770d is the 1.6 branch, which matches the pinned tree.
